o1.biggest_strength: Three distinct angles (blind test, 3 pm desk swap, game-day family) with hooks taken from real comments, and openings ordered by our cost-per-purchase data, so the label never leads.
o1.biggest_mistake: Only Script 2 answers the $3-a-can objection. The other two state the price but never defend it, though price is 15% of comments.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Handle price inside every script, add deliverables, usage rights and a test budget with cut and scale thresholds, so I can send it to creators and run it without extra planning.

o2.biggest_strength: Production-ready package: the three angles tie to cost per purchase and comment shares, price is answered in every script ('12 afternoons for me'), and it covers disclosure, safe zones, rights, timelines and a test budget with cut and scale rules.
o2.biggest_mistake: The spoken disclosure lands mid-scene, most awkwardly during the blind sip in Script 1, and stacks too many words into the 3-10 s window of Script 2. It also runs a little over the word limit.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Move the spoken 'Olipop paid me' to a natural beat after the reveal, and trim Script 2's early lines so they fit the timing.

reason: Both are solid and on-brand, but Output 2 deals with the $3 objection in every ad and gives me the creator rules, rights, deliverables and a test budget with kill and scale rules, so I can hire and launch from it this week.
